content:
Apple's most anticipated product launch event of the year is almost here, with over 10 new products set to debut. Here are the five new Apple products I'm most looking forward to.

iPhone Ultra

The first foldable iPhone is about to launch, combining the iPhone and iPad mini into one — it's truly exciting.

Although there have been plenty of hardware leaks, the software of the iPhone Ultra is really the key to the entire user experience. So I'm eager to see how Apple adapts iOS 27 to run more naturally and powerfully on a foldable display.

I've never tried a foldable smartphone before, but everything I've read says this kind of form factor is the future. Apple clearly thought long and hard before entering the foldable market, and I have high expectations that it will be worth the wait.

HomePad

For years I've been hoping Apple would take the smart home seriously. When Mark Gurman first detailed the upcoming "HomePad" at the end of 2024, it signalled that this shift was coming.

Everything about the HomePad has me excited. Apple Photos slideshow playback, security camera features, Siri AI, Apple Music playback with on-screen lyrics — it all makes me eager to try it out.

The delay to Siri AI has made the wait for the HomePad much longer than expected. But all signs point to an imminent launch, and I'm ready to witness Apple chart the direction of a new smart home era through the HomePad and other new Home products.

Next-generation Apple TV 4K

It's been four years since the last Apple TV 4K launched. The product certainly doesn't need updating every year, but the rise of AI opens up many possibilities for a comprehensive experience overhaul.

I'm eager to see how Siri AI, a more powerful processor, and other hardware and software upgrades can come together to make the Apple TV upgrade worthwhile.

With the next-generation Apple TV 4K launching alongside the HomePad with a camera, I'm also curious whether past rumours of a built-in camera will finally come true. Using FaceTime on the big screen without needing an iPhone would definitely be convenient.

MacBook Ultra

I've been using an iPad Pro as my primary computer for over a decade. The main reason I switched back in 2015 was that the Mac had been falling behind the iPad in hardware and software innovation.

Apple Silicon's arrival on the Mac addressed part of the problem. macOS has also increasingly been updated in sync with iOS and iPadOS. But there are still many aspects of the Mac that feel stuck in the past rather than looking to the future.

I think the MacBook Ultra will change that. Adding touch support, an OLED display, Dynamic Island, a completely new design, and possibly even cellular connectivity — each one is incredibly appealing. This is exactly the Mac refresh I've been waiting for, and I can't wait to see what surprises Apple has in store.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

I haven't decided whether to go for the Series 12 or the Ultra 4 this year. Either way, I'm looking forward to the new models because of one key rumoured upgrade: an entirely new S-series chip designed for the AI era.

Apple Watch chips don't get updated all that often. While Apple tweaks the S-series chip almost every year, meaningful CPU performance gains only come roughly every three years. So there hasn't been a major leap since the S9 in 2023.

But rumours suggest this year's new Apple Watch models will feature a more powerful new chip — the first ever designed for the AI era — which couldn't be more timely as it pairs with the launch of Siri AI.

Which upcoming Apple product are you most excited about? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
